TOO_LARGE. Content-Length is above the type's `max-size` in `device-logs.file-types`,
            10 MB by default.
        '429':
          description: |
            The file may not have been stored. Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost:
            app.log carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are full copies
            every time. One of:

            - KEY_EXISTS: another file of this type from this phone was stored in the same
              millisecond. Nothing is overwritten, and the next upload gets a new receive time
              (ADR 0011).
            - STORAGE_FAILED: S3 failed the write or it ran past its 60 s deadline. Once the whole
              body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the deadline. Never 503.
    head:
      summary: Always 404
      description: Each upload stands alone, so there is never a stored file to compare against.

content.text:
When the S3 write fails or runs past its 60 s deadline, the upload service returns **429 Too Many Requests** with the reason `STORAGE_FAILED`. It must **never return 503**. Overload and storage problems both get 429.

- The 60 s deadline is shorter than the ALB's 120 s idle timeout, so the phone gets the 429 from the service instead of a timeout from the ALB (ADR 0005).
- A 429 doesn't mean the file is missing. Once the whole body has been sent, S3 can still store the object after the deadline.
- Phones don't retry on 429, and no data is lost: `app.log` carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are sent as full copies every time.
- A unit test (`OpenApiDocumentTest.noOperationAnswers503`) checks that the OpenAPI file lists no 503 response.
